name: France
description: Win back Normandy and Aquitaine from the English kings, break Flanders and the south, and drive the English out of France for good.

mission.history: Richard the Lionheart built Château Gaillard on the Seine to guard Normandy, and swore it would hold if its walls were made of butter. Richard is dead, and his brother John is no Richard.
mission.briefing: Storm the Saucy Castle, take Rouen and Caen, and make Normandy French.
mission.victory_text: Rouen opens its gates. After three centuries Normandy belongs to the king of France.
mission.defeat_text: Paris falls, and the Angevins rule from the Somme to the Pyrenees.

mission.history: The Pope has called a crusade against the Cathars of the south, and the barons of the north have gathered at Lyon under Simon de Montfort. Count Raymond of Toulouse protects the heretics.
mission.briefing: March down the Rhône, take Carcassonne and Toulouse, and bring the south under the crown.
mission.victory_text: Carcassonne and Toulouse fall. The south will be French.
mission.defeat_text: The crusade breaks apart, and the south keeps its counts.

events.text: King John lands at La Rochelle to strike from the south.

mission.history: King John, the Emperor Otto and the Count of Flanders have joined against Philip Augustus. Otto and the Flemish march from the north while John lands in Poitou.
mission.briefing: Meet the northern army and break it, then carry the war into Flanders.
mission.victory_text: At Bouvines Otto's eagle falls. John loses Anjou, and the king of France is master in his realm.

mission.history: Hugh of Lusignan has risen in Poitou, and Henry III of England has landed at Royan to help him win back his father's lands.
mission.briefing: Cross the Charente, beat Henry and take Poitou.
mission.victory_text: Henry flees from Taillebourg and Saintes. Poitou is French.
mission.defeat_text: Tours falls, and the Loire is lost.

mission.history: Two years ago the weavers of Flanders cut down the French knights at Courtrai and hung their golden spurs in a church. Philip the Fair has come back with a new army.
mission.briefing: Beat the Flemish militia in the field, then take Ghent and Bruges.
mission.victory_text: The Flemish break at Mons-en-Pévèle, and their cities pay for peace.
mission.defeat_text: Arras falls, and Flanders is lost to the crown.

mission.history: By the Peace of Brétigny the English hold a third of France. Charles V has made the Breton Bertrand du Guesclin Constable of France, and he will not offer them a pitched battle.
mission.briefing: Win Poitou and the Limousin back town by town.
mission.victory_text: Poitiers and La Rochelle are French again, and the English hold little but Bordeaux and Calais.
mission.defeat_text: Paris falls, and Brétigny becomes a beginning, not an end.

events.text: A girl from Domrémy, Joan, has come to the Dauphin at Chinon with a relief force for Orléans.

mission.history: The English and their Burgundian allies hold Paris and the north, and English forts ring Orléans, the last great city on the Loire.
mission.briefing: Hold Orléans for five turns, until the English give up the siege.
mission.victory_text: The English forts burn, and the siege of Orléans is lifted.
mission.defeat_text: Bourges falls, and the Dauphin has nowhere left to go.

mission.history: Orléans is free. Joan says the Dauphin must be crowned at Reims, where French kings have always been crowned, deep in English and Burgundian country.
mission.briefing: Take Troyes and Reims so Charles can be crowned.
mission.victory_text: Charles VII is crowned in Reims cathedral, with Joan beside him.
mission.defeat_text: Orléans falls again, and the coronation never happens.

mission.history: By the Treaty of Arras the Duke of Burgundy has made peace with Charles VII. The English in Paris stand alone, and the city is restless.
mission.briefing: Take Paris back for the king while the English stand alone.
mission.victory_text: The Parisians open the gates, and the English garrison marches out.
mission.defeat_text: Reims falls, and the war turns against France once more.

mission.history: Rouen fell last autumn. Sir Thomas Kyriell has landed at Cherbourg with the last English army in Normandy, and the French guns are ready.
mission.briefing: Destroy Kyriell's army and take the rest of Normandy.
mission.victory_text: At Formigny the French cannon break the longbowmen, and Normandy is French for good.
mission.defeat_text: Rouen falls back to the English.

mission.history: The people of Bordeaux, English for three hundred years, have called back old John Talbot. The French have dug in their guns before Castillon.
mission.briefing: Break Talbot's army and take Bordeaux and Bayonne. Then the Hundred Years' War is over.
mission.victory_text: Talbot dies charging the French guns at Castillon. Of all its French lands England keeps only Calais.
mission.defeat_text: Périgueux falls, and Aquitaine stays English.
